[[File:Greyling 0S.png|thumb|A [[greyling]], an aggressive creature found in the [[Meadows]].]] '''Creatures''' are non-player characters which are found throughout ''[[Valheim (world)|Valheim]]''. They can be split to four categories: * [[Creatures#Bosses|Bosses]] are powerful aggressive creatures that must be summoned. Killing them unlocks [[Forsaken power|Forsaken powers]], increases [[Global Keys|world difficulty]] and provides loot to progress in the game. * [[Creatures#Minibosses|Minibosses]] are unique, named, aggressive creatures that you can find in specific dungeons. Killing any given miniboss will reward with one of [[Hildir's Chests]]. * [[Creatures#Aggressive creatures|Aggressive creatures]] will attack players when alerted. They also drop loot when killed. * [[Creatures#Passive creatures|Passive creatures]] provide resources when killed (or harvested). They will never attack players. * [[Creatures#NPCs|NPCs]] are friendly creatures/characters that cannot be killed and may provide some service or help to the player. == Bosses == Bosses, also known as the '''Forsaken''', can be summoned by offering specific items (hinted by the [[Runestone#Altar Runestones|Runestones]]) at their specific spawn site. They have increased HP and special attacks compared to regular creatures. A boss site is automatically marked on the player's map by reading the runestone in the specific biomes. There are multiple spawn locations for every boss. '''Behavior''' *Creatures will give up chasing after unable to attack for 60 seconds or unable to detect the target for 30 seconds. *Some creatures have a max chase range. After chasing that far they will give up if unable to detect the target for 1 seconds. *After unable to attack for 15 seconds, creatures will focus structures for 15 seconds if they can't reach the target. *Creatures only attack walls and doors if they aren't able to reach the target player. *Some creatures are afraid of fire and will flee from it. *Some creatures try to avoid fire and will be passive near it. *Some creatures circulate around the target while waiting to attack. *Swimming creatures try to flee towards water if forced on ground. *Creatures passively regenerate 1.67% of their max health every minute (100% over 60 minutes). *Creatures gain +30% more effective health per each additional player within 100 meters. E.g. 3 players = +60% effective health. **This is updated whenever the creature takes damage. *Creatures gain +4% more damage per each additional player within 100 meters. Otherwise, No.}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones]] in [[Black Forest#Alternative biomes|Troll Black Forest]]|limit=2|frequency=667|stars=Yes}} }} == Attacks and abilities == Trolls come in two variants: 1/3rd of Trolls are equipped with a log, while the others are unarmed. Unarmed Trolls have three attacks. === Punch === Leans back before swinging to attack the player in a 5-meter 45-degree horizontal arc (60 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 100 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This attack can be used every 4 seconds when within 4 meters of a player. === Ground slam === Lifts both fists up before slamming them down into the ground (70 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 100 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This slam reaches 4.5 meters out in a 90-degree vertical arc, and can be used every 20 seconds when within 5 meters of a player. This effectively means that the Troll will punch five times before doing a slam, assuming that the player is always in range. When the slam hits anything, including the ground, it also creates a 3-meter area that deals 50 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 50 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 30 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage. This area damage is the same at every star level. === Throw === Throws a large boulder at players within 8–20 meters (50 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 60 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). The boulder travels at an initial velocity of 15 meters per second and can travel for 4 seconds before disappearing. It has a spread of 10–20 degrees. This has a cooldown of 10 seconds and can be disabled by standing close to the Troll. Log Trolls have two attacks. === Log swing (vertical) === Slams their log into the ground extending out 9 meters and spanning across 90 degrees (70 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 100 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This attack can be used every 6 seconds when within 8 meters of a player. === Log swing (horizontal) === Swings their log from the side, creating a 10-meter 50-degree arc (60 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 100 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This attack can be used every 6 seconds when within 8 meters of a player. ==Strategy== {{For|strategies for defeating Trolls|Aggressive creature strategies#Troll}} * Among the largest enemies in ''Valheim'', Trolls have a physical strength that reflects their size. Ranged attacks with a Bow or Spear are best and kiting a Troll through dense areas of the forest is very effective, as they have large hitboxes that hinder their pathfinding. * Trolls employ massive yet slow attacks that are easy to avoid but very hard to block and parry. Using a [[Bone Tower Shield]] is effective at blocking most of its attacks, provided the player has sufficient health. ** "Pulling" the attention of a Troll and brandishing a tower shield while other players fire arrow volleys is an effective strategy. * Trolls will sometimes fall into deep ditches or pits, or more often, the large pit at a copper dig site. Their poor pathfinding often renders them stuck. ** If a Troll approaches a ditch that is sufficiently deep (at least 6 meters) and does not fall in, it will not willingly walk in. Unable to reach the player, it will stand still, glowering into the pit. After a few moments, it will turn its aggression towards any player structures it can reach. ** Alternatively, if the positions are reversed, standing atop the ledge of a pit allows for easy dispatch with arrows and spears. * Trolls can spawn with or without a tree trunk in their hand. A Troll equipped with a tree trunk has decidedly better range and destructive power than one that is not. == Notes == * A 1-star Troll has a pale green tint, and a 2-star Troll is tinted a ruddy red. * They are tall (7 meters) and can move along corridors 2 meters and wider. * The curative pollen ejected by [[Greydwarf Shaman]]s also heals Trolls, as they share a [[Factions|Faction]]. * They cannot jump or swim, but they will walk along the bottom of shallow water, sometimes getting a considerable distance from the shore. They can walk through shallow water faster than a player can swim. * All the Troll's attacks (except its rock throw) have a [[Damage#Terrain_damage|tool tier]] of 2, which allows players to use Trolls to harvest resources they are otherwise unable to attain at their current equipment level. Trolls are capable of knocking down and breaking apart [[Oak]] and [[Birch]] trees with their attacks, which is especially useful in the early game for obtaining [[Finewood]] without a [[Bronze Axe]] (or better). See the taming and breeding sections below. == Drops == {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Boar trophy|0star=15%|1star=15%|2star=15%}} {{drop row|item=Leather scraps|0star=1|1star=2|2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Boar meat|0star=1|1star=2|2star=4}}}} == Spawning == {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Anywhere]] in [[Meadows]]|limit=4|stars=After 800 meters from the world center}} {{spawn row|type=1-9 [[spawn points]] near [[Runestone|Boar runestones]]|frequency=0}} {{spawn row|type=0-2 [[spawn points]] near abandoned farms in [[Meadows]]|frequency=0}} {{spawn row|type=From breeding|limit=5, within 10 meters|frequency=-|stars=Inherited from either parent, randomly}} {{spawn row|type=During "Eikthyr rallies the creatures of the forest," [[Events|event]] before defeating [[Eikthyr]]|limit=2|frequency=6|stars=No}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones]] in [[Meadows#Alternative biomes|Peaceful Meadows]]|limit=15|frequency=5|stars=Yes}} }} == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating boars|Aggressive creature strategies#Boar}} === Attack === Swings its head upward and hits in a 45.2-degree horizontal arc with a range of 1.5 meters (10 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] damage). This attack can be used every 5 seconds when within 2 meters of a player. == Taming == ''For general taming information and strategies, see [[Taming]].'' To tame a wild Boar, players should approach while sneaking to avoid alarming it. If a Boar feels threatened, it will become aggressive, chasing the player until they are out of sight, at which point it will revert to a 'hungry' state. Wild Boars have a predictable combat pattern, charging and then retreating, which can be used to the player's advantage when herding them into a pen ''(recommended to tame)''. Constructing a secure pen is essential to prevent the Boar from escaping and to avoid disruption of the taming process by outside sources. To successfully tame a Boar, players need to feed it {{item link|Raspberries}}, {{item link|Blueberries}}, {{item link|Carrot}}s, {{item link|Onion}}s, {{item link|Turnip}}s, or red {{item link|Mushroom}}s. They will ignore all other foods dropped on the ground. Just drop the food on the ground within one meter, and the Boar will eat, as long as it is not frightened ''(indicated by a red exclamation mark)''. Players can place the food on the ground in a stack, as the Boar will only eat one food from the stack at a time. The taming speed is 30 minutes of real-life gameplay with three pieces of food, '''uninterrupted'''; as long as the Boar does not get frightened and the correct amount of food is on the ground, it should only take 30 minutes. A player must remain in the area for taming to progress. If the Boar becomes frightened at any time during taming, the process will take longer and may require more food. == Tamed == When tamed, Boars seek freedom. If a tamed Boar sees an opening in their fenced area, they will run towards it, which can be used to corral them from place to place. Tamed Boars can be renamed by pressing LShift + E. Interacting with them using E will display the message "(Creature name) loves you" on-screen along with a cloud of pink hearts. They are no longer afraid of fire and require feeding for passive health regeneration. Additionally, tamed Boars lose their anchor to their spawn point, allowing them to move more freely. '''Note:''' ''Boars from abandoned farms and Runestones will retain their anchor point and will always try to return home, making them more challenging to handle. It is recommended to either breed these boars on the spot and move the offspring instead, or to name the original tamed animal and then, once bred, kill it. One issue with using the original animal is that it tends to sit in a corner of a pen, staring at its spawn point, which can interfere with breeding as it does not roam the pen.'' == Breeding == Tamed Boars can breed, provided the Boar is happy and well-fed with berries, carrots, onions, turnips or red mushrooms, along with there being another Boar at least within three meters, and no more than five Boars within at least 10 meters. Once the conditions are met, the Boar will accumulate love points (3) with one another until the pregnancy starts. Successful love point is indicated by pink hearts. After gaining enough love points, the Boar becomes pregnant, which is not visualized. After one minute, the Boar gives birth to a baby Boar ''(piglet)'', visualized by a red cloud. Any Boar can become pregnant, which means that if two Boars breed and one becomes pregnant, they still have the ability to breed and get the other pregnant. Once born, the '''piglet''' will take 50 minutes to mature into an adult. Offspring inherit [[Creature Level|stars]] from the parent that gives birth to it. Offspring are tamed at birth and require a [[Butcher Knife]] or friendly fire to kill. '''Forsaken powers''' are unlocked by defeating each boss and hanging their trophy on the [[Sacrificial Stones]]. By default, the player's set forsaken power is activated by [[Controls|pressing F]]. Only one forsaken power can be set at a time, which is changed out at the Sacrificial Stones.

All forsaken powers have a duration of 5 minutes. They also share the same 20-minute cooldown, which does not reset or reduce even when the player logs off, changes their active forsaken power, or sleeps.  

Activating a power locks the player into an animation for a couple of seconds. The player is unable to move or perform any action (with the exception of equipping or unequipping tools/weapons). 

When activating a forsaken power, all players within 10 meters will also receive the benefit of the forsaken power activated. Thus, a party of four players can keep a forsaken power activated virtually indefinitely by consecutively using each player's forsaken power.

'''Ballistae''' are [[:Category:Misc structures|misc structures]] that act as an automated defense. 

A Ballista can hold 40 missiles of the same type, which will be depleted one at a time as it fires. By default, a Ballista will shoot at any [[Creatures|creature]] in an arc (±45 degrees) within a 28 meters range in front of it, including [[Player Character|player characters]] and [[Taming|tamed]] animals. Care should be taken when loading the Ballista, as it will begin shooting after the first missile is loaded if the player is standing within the firing arc.

Damage is solely based upon the [[Missiles|missile]] loaded ([[Wooden Missile]], [[Black Metal Missile]], or [[Flametal Missile]]).

==Targeting==
Targeting can be overridden by using [[trophies]]. The Ballista will usually only target and shoot enemies corresponding to the trophy used, with the exception of Draugr and Charred enemies. 
* Using trophies from [[Draugr]] or [[Draugr Elite]] will set the Ballista to target 'Draugr', including melee and ranged variants, as well as the Draugr Elite. 
* Using trophies from the [[Charred Warrior]], [[Charred Marksman]], or the [[Charred Warlock]] will set the Ballista to target 'Charred', including all of these enemies as well as the [[Charred Twitcher]]. 
* Only one trophy can be active at once, and it is not consumed, allowing for a single trophy to be used on any number of Ballistae. 
* Default targeting can be applied by using the same trophy again, or by dismantling and rebuilding the Ballista.

== Notes ==
* Considering their hostility to friendlies, such as other players and tames, in default targeting mode, caution and placement location is highly advised. Building structures which can be opened and closed, such as [[Wood Structures|wooden doors or wooden gates]], in front of the Ballista to block their field of vision ensures safe passing when needed.
* Ballistae have a slow and inaccurate aim, but quick shooting speed. Building [[Trap|traps]] to immobilize fast-moving enemies in the Ballista's range increase their effectiveness greatly. For bigger and/or slower enemies, the Ballista might need higher elevation to be effective, especially against flying creatures.
* Due to its universal target range, Ballistae can be used to train blocking skills. However, Ballistae ''cannot be parried'', so using [[Shields|tower shields]] in combination with wooden missiles due to lower damage is recommended. They can also serve as protection against other players in multiplayer servers, while still being mindful of the Ballista targeting its owner.
